title: Create oauth.conf nginx include
description:
## What

Create oauth.conf nginx include file containing all OAuth 2.1 location blocks. This file gets deployed to /mnt/appdata/swag/nginx/ (same location as the existing mcp.conf).

Also create the file in the repo under nginx/ so it can be tracked in git and deployed via install.sh or docker volume mount.

## Context

The production configs (arcane.subdomain.conf, gotify.subdomain.conf, etc.) have these OAuth blocks inlined in every config file. That's ~100 lines of duplication per config. Extract them into a single shared include.

The /_oauth_verify internal location points to http://mcp-oauth:8000/verify — this is the mcp-auth.tootie.tv OAuth gateway service running as a Docker container named mcp-oauth.

## What Goes in oauth.conf

Extracted verbatim from arcane.subdomain.conf (the gold standard):

1. /_oauth_verify internal location (proxies to http://mcp-oauth:8000/verify)
2. /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (static JSON, uses  nginx variable)
3. /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/.+ (path-based variant, RFC 9728)
4. /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server → proxy to http://mcp-oauth:8000
5. /.well-known/openid-configuration → proxy to http://mcp-oauth:8000
6. /jwks → proxy to http://mcp-oauth:8000
7. /register → proxy to http://mcp-oauth:8000
8. /authorize → proxy to http://mcp-oauth:8000
9. /token → proxy to http://mcp-oauth:8000
10. /revoke → proxy to http://mcp-oauth:8000
11. /callback → proxy to http://mcp-oauth:8000
12. /success → proxy to http://mcp-oauth:8000
13. error_page 400/401/403 named locations with JSON responses

The /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource static JSON response uses  (nginx variable) so it correctly reflects whichever domain includes this file — no templating needed.

## Decisions

### Locked
- oauth.conf goes in /mnt/appdata/swag/nginx/ (parent of proxy-confs)
- /_oauth_verify proxies to http://mcp-oauth:8000/verify (hardcoded service name)
- Static JSON for /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource uses  and points authorization_servers to https://mcp-auth.tootie.tv
- All other OAuth endpoints proxy to http://mcp-oauth:8000

### Discretion
- Whether to also keep a copy in the repo (nginx/oauth.conf) for version control — recommended yes

## Testing

- [ ] nginx -t passes after including oauth.conf in a test server block
- [ ] /_oauth_verify location is marked internal (cannot be accessed directly)
- [ ] /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource returns correct static JSON with  resolved
- [ ] All proxy locations point to http://mcp-oauth:8000

## Validation

- [ ] File exists at /mnt/appdata/swag/nginx/oauth.conf
- [ ] File is parseable by nginx (nginx -t)
- [ ] All 12 location blocks present
- [ ] Uses  nginx variable (not hardcoded domain)

## Files

- /mnt/appdata/swag/nginx/oauth.conf (create)
- /home/jmagar/code/swag-mcp/nginx/oauth.conf (create in repo for version control)

## Dependencies

None — this is the foundation everything else builds on.

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: FACT: oauth.conf uses nginx $server_name variable for /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource static JSON — works for any domain without templating, no Jinja2 needed in this file

title: Refactor template system: mcp-server templates + oauth.conf + mcp.conf includes
description:
## What

Overhaul the SWAG MCP nginx config template system to match the production gold-standard pattern (arcane.subdomain.conf). The current templates are out of sync with what's actually deployed. 

Replace the three existing templates with two clean, lean templates that delegate OAuth and MCP boilerplate to dedicated nginx include files.

## Why

- Existing templates (swag-compliant-mcp-subdomain.conf.j2, swag-compliant-mcp-subfolder.conf.j2, mcp_location_block.j2) do NOT match the production configs deployed on the host
- /mcp location currently uses auth_method (Authelia) instead of OAuth — Authelia cannot protect MCP servers
- OAuth endpoint location blocks are inlined in templates instead of extracted to a reusable include
- Template naming is verbose and inconsistent

## Target Architecture

Two templates:
- mcp-server.subdomain.conf.j2 — full server block, Authelia on /, OAuth on /mcp
- mcp-server.subfolder.conf.j2 — location block variant

Two nginx includes (live in /mnt/appdata/swag/nginx/):
- mcp.conf — already exists, handles MCP streaming settings
- oauth.conf — NEW, contains all OAuth endpoint location blocks + /_oauth_verify

Result: templates look like standard SWAG sample configs that just include mcp.conf and oauth.conf

## Sources
- File: /mnt/appdata/swag/nginx/proxy-confs/arcane.subdomain.conf — gold standard pattern
- File: /home/jmagar/code/swag-mcp/swag_mcp/core/constants.py:26 — config type constants
- File: /home/jmagar/code/swag-mcp/swag_mcp/services/config_operations.py:202 — template type construction
- File: /home/jmagar/code/swag-mcp/swag_mcp/utils/formatters.py:242 — build_template_filename()
- File: /home/jmagar/code/swag-mcp/swag_mcp/services/mcp_operations.py:322 — hardcoded mcp_location_block.j2
- File: /mnt/appdata/swag/nginx/mcp.conf — existing working include

title: mcp_upstream_port=0 coercion is silent — agent has no feedback about port substitution
description:
## Issue
When `mcp_upstream_port=0` (the default), the dispatch code converts it to `None` via `mcp_upstream_port or None`. The model validator silently substitutes `upstream_port`. The agent receives no indication the substitution occurred — no `ctx.info()`, no response annotation, no log.

Flagged by: kieran-python-reviewer (High), agent-native-reviewer (Warning).

## Severity
P1 CRITICAL (agent-native) — Agents have no way to observe port substitution. An agent that passes `mcp_upstream_port=0` expecting 'inherit' gets the behavior it wants but cannot verify it. Breaks the agent-tool contract: tool must report what it actually did.

## Location
- `swag_mcp/tools/swag.py` — dispatch call: `mcp_upstream_port or None`
- Fix: add `await ctx.info(f'mcp_upstream_port not set, using upstream_port: {upstream_port}')` before dispatch when port is 0/None
- Tool docstring for `mcp_upstream_port`: add 'Use 0 or omit to inherit from upstream_port'

## Why This Matters
- Agent-tool contracts require agents can observe what the tool actually did
- Silent normalization breaks agent's ability to reason about tool outputs
- Schema shows `mcp_upstream_port: int = 0` with no hint that 0 means 'inherit'

## Validation Criteria
- [ ] When `mcp_upstream_port` is 0/None, a note is emitted (ctx.info or response annotation)
- [ ] Note states effective port: 'mcp_upstream_port defaulting to upstream_port: N'
- [ ] Tool docstring for `mcp_upstream_port` states: '0 or omit = inherit from upstream_port'
- [ ] Smoke test section 6b verifies response note appears

## Testing Steps
1. Create: `upstream_app=myapp, upstream_port=8096, mcp_upstream_app=ai-server` (no mcp_upstream_port)
2. Observe tool response — should contain inheritance note
3. Config: `set $mcp_upstream_port "8096";` (inherited correctly)
4. Create with explicit `mcp_upstream_port=9090` — no note, config uses 9090

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: DECISION: Added ctx.info note before dispatch when mcp_upstream_port is 0 and mcp_upstream_app is set. Only emits note for the split-routing case (separate mcp_upstream_app) to avoid noise on simple creates.

title: mcp_upstream_proto not coerced to None at dispatch — bypasses model-validator default inheritance
description:
## Issue
`mcp_upstream_proto` is passed directly as `"http"` (its parameter default) at the dispatch call site without `or None` coercion. The `set_mcp_upstream_defaults` model validator is only triggered by `None` values. Result: when a caller specifies `mcp_upstream_app` but omits `mcp_upstream_proto`, the MCP upstream always gets `http` even when `upstream_proto=https`.

Flagged by: kieran-python-reviewer (Critical).

## Severity
P1 CRITICAL — Silent protocol misconfiguration. If main upstream uses `https` and `mcp_upstream_proto` is not set, the MCP location block silently uses `http`, causing nginx to connect to MCP upstream over wrong protocol with no error to caller.

## Location
- `swag_mcp/tools/swag.py` — dispatch call to `_handle_create_action`, `mcp_upstream_proto` argument
- Fix: pass `mcp_upstream_proto or None` OR change default to `None` instead of `"http"`

## Why This Matters
- `set_mcp_upstream_defaults` model_validator exists specifically to inherit proto from upstream_proto
- Bug bypasses this logic; MCP location block uses wrong protocol silently
- Nginx will fail to connect to HTTPS upstream over HTTP with cryptic SSL errors

## Validation Criteria
- [ ] `mcp_upstream_proto` default changed to `None` in `swag()` tool signature
- [ ] Dispatch passes `mcp_upstream_proto or None` to `_handle_create_action`
- [ ] Test: create with `upstream_proto=https`, no `mcp_upstream_proto` → config has `https` for MCP upstream
- [ ] `set_mcp_upstream_defaults` model validator triggers correctly

## Testing Steps
1. Create: `upstream_app=myapp, upstream_proto=https, mcp_upstream_app=ai-server` (no mcp_upstream_proto)
2. `grep mcp_upstream_proto /mnt/appdata/swag/nginx/proxy-confs/test.subdomain.conf`
3. Before fix: `set $mcp_upstream_proto "http";` (WRONG)
4. After fix: `set $mcp_upstream_proto "https";` (correct — inherited)

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: DECISION: Changed mcp_upstream_proto default from 'http' to None in tool signature. Added 'or None' coercion at dispatch so set_mcp_upstream_defaults model-validator inherits proto from upstream_proto correctly.

title: Remove dead mcp_enabled parameter — all configs already use MCP templates
description:
## Issue
The `mcp_enabled` parameter in the `swag()` tool function has no effect. `config_operations.py` always selects `swag-compliant-mcp-{base_type}` regardless of `mcp_enabled`. Every config gets MCP security features unconditionally.

Flagged by: agent-native-reviewer (Critical), architecture-strategist (High), code-simplicity-reviewer.

## Severity
P1 CRITICAL — Agents passing `mcp_enabled=False` believe they create a non-MCP config but every config silently gets MCP features. The dead parameter creates false documentation.

## Location
- `swag_mcp/tools/swag.py` — `mcp_enabled` parameter in `swag()` and `_handle_create_action()`
- `swag_mcp/services/config_operations.py` — `template_type` always `swag-compliant-mcp-{base_type}`
- `swag_mcp/models/config.py` — `SwagConfigRequest.mcp_enabled` field

## Why This Matters
- Agents cannot opt out of MCP features — no non-MCP template path exists
- Dead parameter creates false documentation in MCP schema
- Agents form wrong mental model about what mcp_enabled controls

## Validation Criteria
- [ ] `mcp_enabled` parameter removed from `swag()` tool signature
- [ ] `SwagConfigRequest.mcp_enabled` field removed or deprecated
- [ ] Tool docstring updated: all configs include MCP-compatible security headers
- [ ] Smoke test section 2a assertions still pass (MCP features unconditionally present)
- [ ] No existing tests rely on `mcp_enabled` as a toggle

## Testing Steps
1. `uv run pytest tests/ -k 'mcp_enabled' -v` — confirm no test depends on toggle behavior
2. Remove parameter, run `uv run pytest` — all tests pass
3. Run smoke-test.sh section 2a — MCP security assertions pass
4. Verify schema: `mcporter list swag-mcp --schema --json` no longer shows `mcp_enabled`

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: DECISION: Removed mcp_enabled from tool signature, model, and tests — confirmed all templates use swag-compliant-mcp-{base_type} unconditionally. Schema docstring updated to clarify MCP headers are always present.

title: backup_action parameter in tool schema not dispatched — sub_action used instead
description:
## Issue
The `backups` action in `swag()` accepts a parameter controlling whether to list or cleanup backups. The tool schema may expose a `backup_action` parameter name while the internal dispatch uses `sub_action`. Agents using the schema-documented parameter name get ignored or an error instead of the correct behavior.

Flagged by: agent-native-reviewer (Warning).

## Severity
P2 IMPORTANT — Agents cannot reliably call the `backups cleanup` sub-action if the parameter name in schema doesn't match what the handler reads. This makes backup cleanup effectively unreachable via schema-guided calls.

## Location
- `swag_mcp/tools/swag.py` — `backups` action handler, parameter name used for sub-action selection
- Check: does the `swag()` tool accept `backup_action` or `sub_action` or both?

## Why This Matters
- Backup cleanup is a critical maintenance operation
- If the parameter name is wrong, agents accumulate .backup files indefinitely
- Inconsistency between documented schema and actual behavior erodes agent trust

## Validation Criteria
- [ ] Confirm the exact parameter name the `backups` handler reads (grep sub_action / backup_action in swag.py)
- [ ] If mismatch: align tool schema parameter name with handler, OR add alias
- [ ] Test: `swag(action='backups', sub_action='cleanup', retention_days=7)` works
- [ ] Test: `swag(action='backups', sub_action='list')` works
- [ ] Schema shows correct parameter name and accepted values

## Testing Steps
1. `grep -n 'backup_action\|sub_action' swag_mcp/tools/swag.py`
2. Call backups cleanup via mcporter: `mcporter call swag-mcp swag '{"action": "backups", "sub_action": "cleanup", "retention_days": 30}'`
3. Call with `backup_action` instead — see which works
4. Align schema and handler to use the same name consistently

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: FACT: backup_action parameter was in schema but NOT passed to _handle_backups_action. Handler re-derived action from retention_days > 0. Fixed: pass backup_action as first arg; handler uses it as primary signal.

title: Split-routing example missing from swag() tool docstring
description:
## Issue
The `swag()` tool docstring documents the basic create action but contains no example showing `upstream_app != mcp_upstream_app` (split-routing). Agents reading the schema have no usage example to follow. The three new `mcp_upstream_*` parameters were added without updating the docstring examples.

Flagged by: agent-native-reviewer (Critical — doc gap).

## Severity
P2 IMPORTANT — Without a concrete example, agents are unlikely to discover or correctly use split-routing. The feature exists and was a significant addition; it needs a clear usage example to be actionable for agents.

## Location
- `swag_mcp/tools/swag.py` — `swag()` function docstring, Action Examples section

## Why This Matters
- Agents derive tool usage from docstring examples, not just parameter descriptions
- Split-routing (main upstream ≠ MCP upstream) is the primary use case for `mcp_upstream_*` params
- Without an example, the feature effectively doesn't exist from an agent perspective

## Validation Criteria
- [ ] Docstring includes a concrete split-routing example with `mcp_upstream_app` different from `upstream_app`
- [ ] Example shows the resulting routing: / → upstream_app:port, /mcp → mcp_upstream_app:port
- [ ] Example explains the use case: 'main app on one server, AI/MCP service on GPU server'
- [ ] `mcporter list swag-mcp --schema --json` description field includes the example

## Testing Steps
1. Read current docstring: grep -A 50 'def swag' swag_mcp/tools/swag.py | head -60
2. Add example under 'create' action examples:
   Example (split-routing): action=create, service_name=jellyfin, upstream_app=jellyfin, upstream_port=8096, mcp_upstream_app=ai-gpu-server, mcp_upstream_port=8080
   Routes: / → jellyfin:8096, /mcp → ai-gpu-server:8080
3. Rebuild container, verify schema shows updated description

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: DECISION: Added split-routing example to swag() docstring showing mcp_upstream_app != upstream_app with explicit routing annotation (/ → upstream_app, /mcp → mcp_upstream_app).

title: EXIT trap backup cleanup in smoke-test.sh incomplete — 4 new test configs not covered
description:
## Issue
The smoke test EXIT trap and preflight cleanup list were not updated when 4 new test configs were added in this session (smoke-quic, smoke-remote-mcp, smoke-authentik, smoke-mcp-sf). If the script exits early (on test failure), these configs remain on disk in `/mnt/appdata/swag/nginx/proxy-confs/`, polluting the SWAG environment for subsequent runs.

Flagged by: pattern-recognition-specialist (Medium).

## Severity
P2 IMPORTANT — Leaked configs from failed runs can interfere with subsequent test runs (false positives on 'config already exists' checks). Also leaves test artifacts in production SWAG config directory.

## Location
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` — EXIT trap at top of script, preflight cleanup section
- Missing: smoke-quic, smoke-remote-mcp, smoke-authentik, smoke-mcp-sf (and their .backup variants)

## Why This Matters
- Smoke test runs against live SWAG — leaked configs get picked up by SWAG on reload
- Subsequent test runs may fail with 'config exists' errors masking real failures
- Consistent cleanup is essential for a reliable test harness

## Validation Criteria
- [ ] EXIT trap lists all 8 (or current count) test configs for deletion
- [ ] Preflight cleanup also removes all 8 configs + their .backup.* variants
- [ ] DRY: both trap and preflight use the same array/function (not duplicate lists)
- [ ] Run script twice in succession — second run starts clean

## Testing Steps
1. Run smoke test, interrupt it mid-way (Ctrl+C during section 7)
2. Check: `ls /mnt/appdata/swag/nginx/proxy-confs/smoke-*` — should be empty after trap fires
3. Before fix: smoke-quic et al remain on disk
4. After fix: all smoke-* configs cleaned up on exit
5. Run smoke test again immediately — no 'already exists' failures

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: FACT: Root cause was duplicate cleanup arrays (eqf.21). Fixed by extracting TEST_CONFIGS array and looping over it in EXIT trap. All 8 test configs now covered including smoke-quic, smoke-remote-mcp, smoke-authentik, smoke-mcp-sf.

title: sleep 1 in swag_reload_check should be a poll loop with timeout
description:
## Issue
The `swag_reload_check` function in `scripts/smoke-test.sh` sends a HUP signal to the SWAG container then sleeps a flat 1 second before checking `nginx -t`. On slow systems or under load, nginx may not have reloaded within 1 second, causing a false negative. On fast systems, the 1-second sleep wastes time unnecessarily.

Flagged by: performance-oracle (P1/High).

## Severity
P2 IMPORTANT — Flat sleep causes flaky test failures on slow CI systems and wastes 1s per reload check. A poll loop is more reliable and faster on average.

## Location
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` — `swag_reload_check` function

## Why This Matters
- CI environments (slower containers) may have nginx reload take > 1s
- A poll loop exits immediately when reload completes, making the test suite faster on average
- Flat sleeps are a known source of CI flakiness

## Validation Criteria
- [ ] `swag_reload_check` replaced with poll loop: check `nginx -t` every 0.5s up to 10s timeout
- [ ] On fast systems, test completes in < 1s (no wasted time)
- [ ] On slow systems, test waits up to 10s before failing
- [ ] Timeout failure message is clear: 'SWAG nginx did not reload within 10s'

## Testing Steps
1. View current `swag_reload_check` implementation in `scripts/smoke-test.sh`
2. Replace `sleep 1; nginx -t` with poll loop (while loop, counter, sleep 0.5)
3. Run section 3 of smoke test — confirm it passes and completes faster than before
4. Simulate slow reload (add artificial delay) — confirm 10s timeout triggers correctly

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: DECISION: Replaced sleep 1 with poll loop (20 × 0.5s = 10s timeout) in swag_reload_check. Fast exits on success, explicit timeout failure message.

title: Nginx validation bypass in SSH mode — local nginx -t cannot validate remote SWAG config
description:
## Issue
The smoke test and internal validation use `docker exec swag nginx -t` to validate nginx syntax after config creation. When `SWAG_MCP_PROXY_CONFS_PATH` is an SSH URI (remote SWAG), this validation is skipped or falls back to local nginx which may be a different version. Remote SWAG may have different nginx modules compiled in, reject directives the local nginx accepts, or vice versa.

Flagged by: architecture-strategist (High).

## Severity
P2 IMPORTANT — SSH mode is a supported feature but its nginx validation is weaker than local mode. A config created for a remote SWAG could have syntax errors that are only caught when remote SWAG reloads (causing downtime).

## Location
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` — `assert_nginx_valid()` function — assumes local `swag` container
- `swag_mcp/services/config_operations.py` — post-create validation step (if any)
- Fix: in SSH mode, run `nginx -t` on the remote host via SSH exec, not local docker exec

## Why This Matters
- Remote SWAG may run a different nginx version with different module support
- A directive valid locally (e.g., `quic`) may require a specific nginx build flag on the remote host
- Config creation succeeds, remote SWAG fails to reload, service outage with no local error

## Validation Criteria
- [ ] SSH mode: nginx validation executes via SSH exec on remote host (or via docker exec on remote docker)
- [ ] OR: SSH mode documents explicitly that nginx validation is skipped and why
- [ ] Smoke test `assert_nginx_valid()` documents the SSH limitation
- [ ] Remote nginx version check added to connection diagnostics

## Testing Steps
1. Set `SWAG_MCP_PROXY_CONFS_PATH=ssh://user@host/path` in test env
2. Create a config with an invalid directive for remote nginx
3. Verify the validation catches it (before fix: validation passes locally, remote SWAG fails)
4. After fix: validation runs on remote host, catches the mismatch

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: DECISION: Added isinstance(self.fs, SSHFilesystem) check before nginx -t in mcp_operations.py. In SSH mode, local nginx cannot validate remote configs — logs WARNING and skips rather than falsely passing.

title: mcp_upstream_app missing pattern constraint in tool schema
description:
## Issue
The `mcp_upstream_app` parameter added to the `swag()` tool function in this branch is defined as a plain `str` with only `max_length=100` — no `pattern` constraint. The model-level `SwagConfigRequest.mcp_upstream_app` field has a validator (`validate_mcp_upstream_app`) but that runs after the tool schema layer. An agent could pass a value that passes the tool schema but fails Pydantic validation later.

Flagged by: security-sentinel (Medium).

## Severity
P2 IMPORTANT — Defense-in-depth gap. Tool schema should reject obviously invalid values before they reach model validation. Without a pattern constraint, the MCP schema exposed to agents does not communicate the format requirements.

## Location
- `swag_mcp/tools/swag.py` — `mcp_upstream_app` Annotated field definition
- Fix: add `pattern=r'^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]*$'` (or match `VALID_UPSTREAM_PATTERN`) to the Annotated Field

## Why This Matters
- Schema-level constraints are the primary communication channel to agents about valid values
- Agents read the schema to know what to pass; missing pattern means agents get no format guidance
- Consistent with how `upstream_app` parameter is already defined with a pattern constraint

## Validation Criteria
- [ ] `mcp_upstream_app` Annotated field includes `pattern` matching `upstream_app` format
- [ ] `mcporter list swag-mcp --schema --json` shows pattern constraint for `mcp_upstream_app`
- [ ] Invalid value (e.g., `mcp_upstream_app='invalid;value'`) rejected at schema level
- [ ] Valid values (hyphenated hostnames, IPs) still accepted

## Testing Steps
1. Check current schema: `mcporter list swag-mcp --schema --json | jq '.tools[] | select(.name=="swag") | .inputSchema.properties.mcp_upstream_app'`
2. Add pattern to Annotated Field definition
3. Rebuild container and re-check schema
4. Attempt call with invalid value — should fail at schema validation

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: DECISION: Added pattern=VALID_UPSTREAM_PATTERN.replace('+', '*') to mcp_upstream_app Field in tool signature, matching existing upstream_app pattern. The replace makes it optional (empty string ok since it defaults to upstream_app).

title: Divergent inline regex in config_operations.py vs VALID_UPSTREAM_PATTERN — rejects valid hostnames
description:
## Issue
`config_operations.py` contains an inline regex for upstream validation that differs from the `VALID_UPSTREAM_PATTERN` constant defined in `core/constants.py`. The inline pattern `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+` is stricter (or different) than the centralized pattern, causing valid container names (hyphenated names, IPv6 addresses) to be inconsistently accepted or rejected depending on which code path is used.

Flagged by: security-sentinel (Medium).

## Severity
P2 IMPORTANT — Inconsistent validation creates unpredictable behavior. Users get different rejection/acceptance outcomes for the same upstream value depending on which function is called. Security audit of validation patterns is made harder by divergence.

## Location
- `swag_mcp/services/config_operations.py` — inline upstream regex pattern
- `swag_mcp/core/constants.py` — `VALID_UPSTREAM_PATTERN` (the canonical source)
- Fix: replace all inline upstream patterns with `import VALID_UPSTREAM_PATTERN from constants`

## Why This Matters
- Single source of truth for validation patterns prevents drift
- Hyphenated container names (e.g., `ai-gpu-server`) are common in Docker Compose
- IPv6 upstream support is documented but may be rejected by the inline pattern

## Validation Criteria
- [ ] `config_operations.py` imports and uses `VALID_UPSTREAM_PATTERN` (no inline duplicate)
- [ ] `VALID_UPSTREAM_PATTERN` in constants.py covers: alphanumeric, hyphens, dots, underscores, IPv4, IPv6
- [ ] Test: create config with `upstream_app=ai-gpu-server-v2` (hyphenated) — succeeds
- [ ] Test: create config with `upstream_app=192.168.1.100` (IPv4) — succeeds
- [ ] Run `uv run pytest tests/test_validators_coverage.py -v` — all pass

## Testing Steps
1. Grep for inline patterns: `grep -n 'a-zA-Z0-9\.' swag_mcp/services/config_operations.py`
2. Compare with `VALID_UPSTREAM_PATTERN` in constants.py
3. Try creating: `upstream_app=my-hyphenated-container` — should succeed
4. After fix: all upstream validation uses single canonical pattern

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: FACT: config_operations.py had inline r'^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$' that didn't match VALID_UPSTREAM_PATTERN (r'^[a-zA-Z0-9_.\[\]:-]+$'). The inline pattern rejected IPv6 brackets and colons. Replaced with import of VALID_UPSTREAM_PATTERN.

title: Upstream re-validation gap in add_mcp path — extracted values not re-validated before template use
description:
## Issue
In `config_updaters.py`, the `add_mcp` update path extracts upstream values from the existing config file via regex pattern matching. These extracted values are passed directly to the template renderer without re-running Pydantic field validators (e.g., `VALID_UPSTREAM_PATTERN`). If the config file was manually edited to contain malformed values, they bypass validation.

Flagged by: security-sentinel (Medium).

## Severity
P2 IMPORTANT — Template injection risk if malformed upstream values are in existing config. The template renders these values as nginx variables (`set $upstream_app ...`) — a crafted value could break nginx syntax or escape the variable context.

## Location
- `swag_mcp/services/config_updaters.py` — `add_mcp` path, regex extraction of upstream values
- Fix: re-validate extracted upstream_app/port/proto through `validate_upstream_app()` before passing to template

## Why This Matters
- Manual edits to configs are common in SWAG setups
- A malformed upstream value in an existing config could cause the add_mcp operation to generate an invalid nginx config
- No re-validation means the template is the last line of defense

## Validation Criteria
- [ ] Extracted upstream_app value validated against `VALID_UPSTREAM_PATTERN` before template render
- [ ] Extracted upstream_port validated as integer in 1-65535 range
- [ ] If validation fails, return clear error message (not a corrupted nginx config)
- [ ] Test: create config, manually edit upstream to invalid value, attempt add_mcp — should error, not corrupt

## Testing Steps
1. Create a config: `smoke-addmcp.subdomain.conf`
2. Manually set upstream_app to `invalid;inject` in the file
3. Call: `swag update config_name=smoke-addmcp.subdomain.conf update_field=add_mcp update_value=/mcp`
4. Expected: error 'Invalid upstream_app in existing config'
5. Before fix: template renders the injected value, nginx -t may fail or be exploited

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: DECISION: Added re-validation of extracted upstream_app (VALID_UPSTREAM_PATTERN) and upstream_port (1-65535 range) in mcp_operations.py add_mcp path, before template render. Guards against manually-edited configs with injected values.

title: Backup file on-disk verification: assert .backup.* files exist before removal
description:
## What

After any operation with `create_backup:true`, glob for backup files matching the config name in the proxy-confs directory and assert at least one exists before calling remove. Currently the test never verifies backups were actually written.

## Context

Backup file naming convention (confirmed live):
```
{config_name}.backup.{timestamp}_{uuid}
# e.g. axon.subdomain.conf.backup.20260325_014325_884332_76f133e4
```

Backup files live alongside configs in:
`/mnt/appdata/swag/nginx/proxy-confs/`

```bash
assert_backup_exists() {
    local config_name="$1"
    local backup_dir="/mnt/appdata/swag/nginx/proxy-confs"
    local count
    count=$(ls "${backup_dir}/${config_name}.backup."* 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
    if [[ "$count" -gt 0 ]]; then
        pass "backup file exists for $config_name ($count file(s))"
    else
        fail "no backup file found for $config_name in $backup_dir"
    fi
}

cleanup_test_backups() {
    local config_name="$1"
    rm -f "/mnt/appdata/swag/nginx/proxy-confs/${config_name}.backup."* 2>/dev/null || true
}
```

3. Section 10 REMOVE — call remove with create_backup:true, assert backup file created

title: Real 2xx health check: parse status code from health_check response and assert range
description:
## What

Enhance section 9 (HEALTH CHECK) to parse the HTTP status code from the health_check response text and assert it falls within 2xx or 3xx range. Currently the test only checks the call didn't crash — it doesn't verify the domain returned a success code.

## Context

Live health_check response format:
- Success: `✅ None - 200 (812.0ms)`
- Success with redirect: `✅ domain - 301 (50ms)`  
- Failure: `❌ domain - error message`

Parse pattern:
```bash
assert_http_success() {
    local output="$1" label="$2"
    # Extract status code: look for pattern '- NNN ('
    local code
    code=$(echo "$output" | grep -oP '(?<=- )\d{3}(?= )' | head -1)
    if [[ -z "$code" ]]; then
        fail "$label — could not parse status code from: $(echo "$output" | head -1)"
        return
    fi
    if [[ "$code" -ge 200 && "$code" -lt 400 ]]; then
        pass "$label — HTTP $code"
    else
        fail "$label — got HTTP $code (expected 2xx/3xx)"
    fi
}
```

Section 9 uses `swag.tootie.tv` which returned 200 live. Section 9a uses a nonexistent domain — assert it returns ❌ (failure is the expected outcome).

## Decisions

### Locked
- Accept 2xx AND 3xx as success (redirects are valid proxy behavior)
- Use grep -oP for status code extraction (bash-native, no jq needed)
- Section 9a (invalid domain) should assert ❌ in response (not assert_http_success)

### Discretion
- Whether to add a second known-good domain as fallback if swag.tootie.tv is unreachable (recommend: add skip logic — if curl to domain fails from host, mark as skipped not failed)

## Testing

- [ ] Status code 200 extracted correctly from '✅ None - 200 (812.0ms)'
- [ ] Status code 301 extracted correctly from '✅ domain - 301 (50ms)'
- [ ] Missing status code (parse failure) triggers FAIL with helpful message
- [ ] swag.tootie.tv health check asserts 2xx/3xx (not just 'call completed')
- [ ] Section 9a (nonexistent domain) asserts ❌ in response (failure is correct)
- [ ] Unreachable domain from host environment skips gracefully with SKIP not FAIL

## Validation

- [ ] Section 9 now has 2 assertions: call completes + status code in 2xx/3xx
- [ ] Section 9a has 2 assertions: call completes + response contains ❌

## Files

- scripts/smoke-test.sh — add assert_http_success() helper, update sections 9 and 9a

## Dependencies

None — uses existing mcp() helper and section 9/9a structure

## References

- Live health_check result: '✅ None - 200 (812.0ms)' (confirmed with swag.tootie.tv)
- File: swag_mcp/tools/swag.py:778 — health_check result formatting

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: FACT: health_check response format is '✅ None - 200 (812.0ms)' — grep -oP '(?<=- )\d{3}(?= )' extracts the 3-digit status code. Domain that's unreachable produces '❌' — assert for ❌ on invalid domains (that's the CORRECT outcome).

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: DECISION: Accept 2xx AND 3xx as success (200-399 range). Redirects are valid proxy behavior and the health_check follows them.

title: SWAG reload verification: HUP signal after create, confirm nginx picks up config
description:
## What

After creating a config, send HUP to the SWAG container to trigger nginx graceful reload, then confirm nginx is still healthy. This verifies SWAG actually loads new configs into the running server — not just that the file exists.

## Context

```bash
swag_reload_check() {
    local label="$1"
    # Send HUP for graceful reload
    if docker kill --signal=HUP swag 2>&1 | grep -q '^swag$'; then
        # Brief pause for reload to complete (nginx graceful = drain connections)
        sleep 1
        # Confirm still healthy post-reload
        if docker exec swag nginx -t 2>&1 | grep -q 'test is successful'; then
            pass "SWAG reloaded successfully: $label"
        else
            fail "SWAG reload broke nginx: $label"
        fi
    else
        fail "HUP signal failed: $label"
    fi
}
```

`docker kill --signal=HUP swag` returns the container name on success (confirmed live). After HUP, nginx gracefully reloads — worker processes finish current requests then restart. 1s sleep is sufficient for smoke test purposes.

Call after: section 2 CREATE (after nginx_syntax_check), section 6 CREATE MCP (after nginx_syntax_check).

## Decisions

### Locked
- docker kill --signal=HUP swag (confirmed working live)
- sleep 1 between HUP and validation (minimal wait, smoke test not load test)
- Verify reload by re-running nginx -t (not by hitting the domain — domain may not be reachable)
- Call only after CREATE operations, not after every UPDATE (too frequent for smoke test)

### Discretion
- Whether to add a curl to localhost to confirm nginx is still serving (recommend: skip, nginx -t is sufficient)

## Testing

- [ ] swag_reload_check called after section 2 CREATE
- [ ] swag_reload_check called after section 6 CREATE MCP
- [ ] Pass when HUP succeeds and nginx -t passes
- [ ] Fail when nginx -t fails post-reload (broken config scenario)
- [ ] Graceful skip if docker not available

## Validation

- [ ] Both CREATE sections trigger reload verification
- [ ] nginx -t passes post-reload for both standard and MCP configs
- [ ] No lingering reload state after test cleanup

## Files

- scripts/smoke-test.sh — add swag_reload_check() helper, call in sections 2 and 6

## Dependencies

- swag-mcp-eqf.2 (nginx syntax validation) — reload check reuses nginx -t, define helper there first

## References

- Live test: docker kill --signal=HUP swag → outputs 'swag'
- SWAG graceful reload: drains connections before restarting workers

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: FACT: docker kill --signal=HUP swag returns container name 'swag' on success. sleep 1 + nginx -t is sufficient to confirm nginx is healthy post-reload for smoke test purposes (nginx drains connections, not restarted).

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: DECISION: swag_reload_check() is advisory — skips gracefully if docker not available. It does NOT roll back on failure since the HUP already happened; the test reports the failure and continues.

title: nginx syntax validation: docker exec swag nginx -t after create/edit
description:
## What

After every create and edit operation in the smoke test, run `docker exec swag nginx -t` and assert it exits 0. This confirms the generated nginx config is syntactically valid — not just that the file was written.

## Context

`docker exec swag nginx -t` validates ALL configs in /config/nginx/ including proxy-confs. Exit code 0 = valid, non-zero = syntax error. Stderr output includes the failing file path.

```bash
nginx_syntax_check() {
    local label="$1"
    if docker exec swag nginx -t 2>&1 | grep -q 'test is successful'; then
        pass "nginx syntax valid: $label"
    else
        fail "nginx syntax error after $label"
        docker exec swag nginx -t 2>&1 | grep -v '^$' | head -5 | sed 's/^/    /'
    fi
}
```

Call after: CREATE (section 2), EDIT (section 5), CREATE MCP (section 6), and UPDATE add_mcp (section 4d).

## Decisions

### Locked
- Use docker exec swag nginx -t (confirmed working: exits 0, outputs 'test is successful')
- Check after CREATE, EDIT, CREATE MCP, and UPDATE add_mcp
- Do NOT check after UPDATE port/upstream/app — those do text substitution and nginx -t after add_mcp covers it

### Discretion
- Whether to also check after remove (empty file = no nginx syntax error to check, skip)

## Testing

- [ ] nginx_syntax_check called after section 2 CREATE standard subdomain
- [ ] nginx_syntax_check called after section 4d UPDATE add_mcp
- [ ] nginx_syntax_check called after section 5 EDIT full replacement
- [ ] nginx_syntax_check called after section 6 CREATE MCP config
- [ ] Failure shows nginx error output (not just 'failed')
- [ ] Handles docker not running gracefully (skip with warning)

## Validation

- [ ] All 4 nginx -t calls pass against the actual running SWAG container
- [ ] A deliberately broken config (injected bad syntax) triggers a FAIL assertion

## Files

- scripts/smoke-test.sh — add nginx_syntax_check() helper, insert calls at 4 points

## Dependencies

None — uses docker directly, not the swag tool

## References

- Live test: docker exec swag nginx -t → 'nginx: configuration file /etc/nginx/nginx.conf syntax is ok'
- SWAG container name: swag (confirmed via docker ps)

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: FACT: docker exec swag nginx -t validates ALL 494 configs simultaneously, not just the modified one. A broken config in /proxy-confs/ causes all subsequent nginx_syntax_checks to fail cascade-style until it's fixed or removed.

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: PATTERN: nginx_syntax_check() outputs the first 5 non-blank lines of nginx -t stderr when failing — sufficient to identify the offending file and line without overwhelming output.

title: Schema validation: compare live MCP schema against expected spec
description:
## What

Fetch the live MCP tool schema from the server via JSON-RPC `tools/list`, parse it, and assert it matches a hardcoded expected specification. Fail loudly if any field is missing, has the wrong type, wrong default, or the action enum drifts.

## Context

The server exposes its schema via:
```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8012/mcp -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
```
Response is SSE: `event: message\ndata: {json}\n\n`. Extract the data line, parse JSON, navigate to `result.tools[0].inputSchema`.

Expected schema snapshot (live 2026-03-30):
- action: enum [list,create,view,edit,update,remove,logs,backups,health_check], required
- list_filter: enum [all,active,samples], default=all
- upstream_proto: enum [http,https], default=http
- log_type: enum [nginx-access,nginx-error,fail2ban,letsencrypt,renewal], default=nginx-error
- backup_action: enum [cleanup,list], default=list
- upstream_port: integer, default=0
- mcp_enabled: boolean, default=false
- create_backup: boolean, default=true
- lines: integer, default=50
- timeout: integer, default=30
- update_field: anyOf with enum [port,upstream,app,add_mcp]
- All 21 properties present

## Decisions

### Locked
- Use bash + python3 for JSON parsing (already used in script for json escaping)
- Schema fetched via direct curl JSON-RPC call (mcporter --json doesn't expose schema cleanly)
- Fail = print diff of expected vs actual, increment FAIL counter

### Discretion
- Whether to warn on extra fields or fail hard (recommend: warn only)
- How granular to check defaults (recommend: check all enum fields + required array)

## Testing

- [ ] Assert tool name is "swag"
- [ ] Assert action enum contains exactly: list,create,view,edit,update,remove,logs,backups,health_check (no more, no less)
- [ ] Assert action is in required array
- [ ] Assert list_filter enum = [all,active,samples]
- [ ] Assert upstream_proto enum = [http,https]
- [ ] Assert log_type enum = [nginx-access,nginx-error,fail2ban,letsencrypt,renewal]
- [ ] Assert backup_action enum = [cleanup,list]
- [ ] Assert update_field contains enum [port,upstream,app,add_mcp]
- [ ] Assert all 21 property names present
- [ ] Assert integer fields (upstream_port, lines, timeout, retention_days) have type integer
- [ ] Assert boolean fields (mcp_enabled, create_backup, enable_quic, follow_redirects) have type boolean

## Validation

- [ ] Script fails with clear diff output when action enum has an unknown value
- [ ] Script passes when schema matches exactly
- [ ] Handles curl failure gracefully (server down = skip with warning, not crash)

## Files

- scripts/smoke-test.sh — add schema_check() function and call it in section 0 (before preflight)

## Dependencies

None — runs first, independent of other sections

## References

- Live endpoint: POST http://localhost:8012/mcp, method tools/list
- File: swag_mcp/models/enums.py — SwagAction source of truth
- File: swag_mcp/tools/swag.py:155-281 — parameter definitions

comments.author: Jacob Magar
Jacob Magar
comments.text: DECISION: Reduced schema assertions to 3 (tool name, action enum exact match, action is required) per engineering review — exhaustive 21-property checks are brittle and slow. The 3 assertions cover drift detection adequately.

title: Upgrade smoke-test.sh to full live end-to-end integration test suite
description:
## Overview

Enhance `scripts/smoke-test.sh` from a string-match smoke test into a genuine live integration test that validates nginx config correctness, SWAG reload, backup files on disk, real HTTP 2xx status codes, schema drift, auth method output, and subfolder routing — all via mcporter calls against the live server.

## Current State

- 45 passing assertions across 10 sections
- All assertions are string-match on mcporter text output or file existence checks
- Does NOT verify: nginx syntax, SWAG reload, 2xx HTTP codes, backup files written, schema drift, auth directives, subfolder routing

## What Changes

Seven distinct verification layers added to the existing 45-test baseline:

1. **Schema validation** — fetch live MCP schema via JSON-RPC tools/list, compare against hardcoded expected spec
2. **nginx syntax validation** — docker exec swag nginx -t after every create/edit
3. **SWAG reload verification** — HUP signal after create, confirm nginx -t still passes
4. **Real 2xx health check assertions** — parse status code from health_check response, assert 2xx/3xx
5. **Backup file on-disk verification** — glob for .backup.* files before removal, assert count > 0
6. **Auth method validation** — authelia config includes authelia-server.conf + authelia-location.conf; none config has no authelia includes
7. **Subfolder routing validation** — location ^~ path blocks present, no dedicated server_name

## Key Facts

- SWAG container: swag (lscr.io/linuxserver/swag)
- swag-mcp container: swag-mcp
- proxy-confs: /mnt/appdata/swag/nginx/proxy-confs
- Backup naming: {config}.backup.{timestamp}_{uuid}
- docker exec swag nginx -t exits 0 on success
- docker kill --signal=HUP swag triggers graceful reload
- health_check response format: ✅ None - 200 (812.0ms)
- authelia generates: authelia-server.conf + authelia-location.conf includes
- subfolder location pattern: location ^~ /service-name (no dedicated server_name)

## Sources

- File: scripts/smoke-test.sh — existing 45-test baseline
- File: swag_mcp/tools/swag.py — tool parameter definitions
- File: templates/swag-compliant-mcp-subdomain.conf.j2 — MCP template
- Live: http://localhost:8012/mcp tools/list schema snapshot 2026-03-30
- Investigation: nginx -t, HUP reload, backup naming, authelia/subfolder patterns confirmed live

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: LEARNED: mcp_enabled parameter in swag() tool has ZERO effect — config_operations.py always uses swag-compliant-mcp-{base_type} template regardless of its value. All configs get MCP security headers unconditionally. Dead parameters in MCP tool schemas cause agents to form wrong mental models about what the tool does.

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: PATTERN: When coercing tool parameters to None to trigger model validators, ALL parameters in the set must be coerced consistently — mcp_upstream_app and mcp_upstream_port used 'or None' but mcp_upstream_proto did not, bypassing the model validator for protocol inheritance.

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: LEARNED: Silent parameter normalization in MCP tools breaks the agent-tool contract. When a tool silently substitutes a default value for a parameter the agent passed, it must emit ctx.info() or annotate the response — otherwise agents cannot reason about what the tool actually did.

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: LEARNED: In FastMCP tools with split-routing features, if the parent feature (mcp_upstream_*) was added to the model layer but never exposed in the tool schema, the feature is effectively unreachable by agents for months — the smoke test surfaced this bug by trying to actually call it.

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: PATTERN: Upstream validation must be centralized — divergent inline regex patterns vs canonical VALID_UPSTREAM_PATTERN constant cause inconsistent accept/reject behavior for the same input. Always import from the constant, never duplicate the pattern inline.

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: LEARNED: nginx -t in SSH/remote mode runs against local nginx version which may differ from the remote SWAG nginx build — a config valid locally can fail to reload on the remote host with no local error signal. Always validate against the actual target nginx.

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: PATTERN: Flat sleep() before async check (sleep 1; nginx -t) is a known CI flakiness source. Replace with poll loop: check every N ms up to timeout. Tests complete faster on fast systems and are more reliable on slow ones.

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: LEARNED: EXIT traps and preflight cleanup lists that enumerate test config names are a DRY violation — adding a new test config in one place (smoke test body) without updating both the EXIT trap and preflight list leaves leaked artifacts in production SWAG config dir on test failure.

title: Section 11 inline nginx syntax check should use assert_nginx_valid() helper
description:
## Issue
Section 11 of `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (subfolder routing validation) contains an inline `docker exec swag nginx -t` check rather than calling the `assert_nginx_valid()` helper used elsewhere. This is inconsistent and means section 11 nginx failures produce different error messages than other sections.

Flagged by: code-simplicity-reviewer.

## Severity
P3 NICE-TO-HAVE — Cosmetic consistency issue. Harder to read and maintain than using the established helper.

## Location
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` — Section 11, inline nginx -t check

## Validation Criteria
- [ ] Section 11 calls `assert_nginx_valid "smoke-subfolder section"` instead of inline docker exec
- [ ] Error messages from section 11 nginx failures match format from other sections
- [ ] All nginx validation sections use the same helper

## Testing Steps
1. `grep -n 'nginx -t' scripts/smoke-test.sh` — find all occurrences
2. Confirm only section 11 is inline (not using helper)
3. Replace with `assert_nginx_valid` call
4. Run section 11 — output format matches other sections

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: DECISION: Replaced inline docker exec nginx -t blocks in sections 11 and 11a with nginx_syntax_check helper calls. Error messages now consistent with all other sections.

title: Duplicate cleanup arrays in smoke-test.sh — extract remove_all_test_configs helper
description:
## Issue
The EXIT trap and the preflight cleanup section in `scripts/smoke-test.sh` both enumerate the full list of test config names for deletion. This is a DRY violation: when a new test config is added, two places must be updated (and the missing update in this session caused bead swag-mcp-eqf.16).

Flagged by: code-simplicity-reviewer.

## Severity
P3 NICE-TO-HAVE — DRY violation that is the root cause of swag-mcp-eqf.16 (incomplete EXIT trap). Fixing this prevents future recurrence.

## Location
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` — EXIT trap definition and preflight cleanup section

## Validation Criteria
- [ ] Single `TEST_CONFIGS` array defined once at top of script
- [ ] Both EXIT trap and preflight cleanup iterate over `TEST_CONFIGS`
- [ ] Adding a new config requires only updating `TEST_CONFIGS` array
- [ ] Script behavior unchanged (all configs cleaned up in both paths)

## Testing Steps
1. Define: `TEST_CONFIGS=(smoke-test smoke-noauth smoke-quic smoke-remote-mcp smoke-authelia smoke-authentik smoke-subfolder smoke-mcp-sf)`
2. EXIT trap: `for c in "${TEST_CONFIGS[@]}"; do rm -f ...; done`
3. Preflight: same loop
4. Run smoke test, interrupt, verify cleanup — then run again, verify clean start

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: DECISION: Extracted TEST_CONFIGS array at top of smoke-test.sh. Both EXIT trap and cleanup section now iterate over it. Adding a new test config only requires updating the array.

title: Circular import workaround in config_updaters.py should be refactored
description:
## Issue
`config_updaters.py` contains a workaround for a circular import (importing inside a function or using TYPE_CHECKING guard). This is a code smell indicating the service module boundary isn't clean.

Flagged by: architecture-strategist (Medium).

## Severity
P3 NICE-TO-HAVE — Functions correctly but the workaround is fragile and makes the import graph harder to reason about.

## Location
- `swag_mcp/services/config_updaters.py` — circular import workaround

## Validation Criteria
- [ ] Circular dependency resolved via proper module restructuring or shared interface
- [ ] No function-level imports or TYPE_CHECKING workarounds for the circular dep
- [ ] `uv run ty check swag_mcp/` passes cleanly

## Testing Steps
1. `grep -n 'TYPE_CHECKING\|import.*inside\|# circular' swag_mcp/services/config_updaters.py`
2. Identify the cycle, restructure to break it
3. `uv run pytest tests/ -v` — all pass after restructure

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: DECISION: Replaced MCPOperations wrapper class in config_updaters.py with MCPOperationsProtocol (Protocol). swag_manager.py now passes self.mcp_operations directly to ConfigFieldUpdaters, eliminating the circular import entirely. TYPE_CHECKING guard removed.

title: PROXY_CONFS_DIR hardcoded in smoke-test.sh — should be env-configurable
description:
## Issue
`scripts/smoke-test.sh` hardcodes `PROXY_CONFS_DIR=/mnt/appdata/swag/nginx/proxy-confs`. Any user with SWAG mounted at a different path cannot run the smoke test without editing the script.

Flagged by: security-sentinel/architecture-strategist.

## Severity
P3 NICE-TO-HAVE — The smoke test currently only runs correctly in this specific environment. Parameterizing makes it reusable.

## Location
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` — top of file, `PROXY_CONFS_DIR` variable

## Validation Criteria
- [ ] `PROXY_CONFS_DIR` read from environment, fallback to current hardcoded default
- [ ] README or script header documents the env var
- [ ] `PROXY_CONFS_DIR=/custom/path bash scripts/smoke-test.sh` works

## Testing Steps
1. `PROXY_CONFS_DIR=/tmp/test-confs bash scripts/smoke-test.sh` (after setup)
2. Verify configs created in custom path

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: DECISION: Changed PROXY_CONFS_DIR to use ${PROXY_CONFS_DIR:-/mnt/appdata/swag/nginx/proxy-confs} pattern. Preserves default for existing users, allows override via env var.

title: Section numbering gap in smoke-test.sh — no section 4a, inconsistent labeling
description:
## Issue
The smoke test section numbering has gaps (e.g., jumps from 4 to 5 with no 4a) and some sections use letter suffixes (2a, 2b, 6b, 7b, 7c, 11b) while others use plain numbers. Inconsistent labeling makes it hard to reference specific sections in bug reports.

Flagged by: pattern-recognition-specialist.

## Severity
P3/P4 NICE-TO-HAVE — Cosmetic only, no functional impact.

## Location
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` — all section header comments

## Validation Criteria
- [ ] Sections numbered consistently (either all use sub-letters or all use sequential integers)
- [ ] No numbering gaps

## Testing Steps
1. `grep -n '^# ==== SECTION' scripts/smoke-test.sh` — list all section headers
2. Renumber consistently
3. Update any cross-references in comments

comments.author: Jacob Magar
comments.text: DECISION: Renumbered 4b→4a (upstream update), 6b→6a (remote MCP), 11b→11a (mcp-subfolder). Section 4d kept with annotation explaining the gap. Section 6 description updated to drop mcp_enabled reference.
